sections.h2: Who to call about a tax question
sections.html:
Tax matters in the county run through Clayton, where three offices share the building at 41 South Central Avenue. One values real estate and personal property (the Assessor). One hears disputes about those values (the Board of Equalization). The third, the Collector of Revenue inside the Department of Revenue, issues bills and receives payment.

St. Louis County tax offices in Clayton
OfficePhoneEmailHours
Assessor, 3rd floor314-615-2555Assessor@stlouiscountymo.govCounter Mon to Thu 8:00 to 3:30; phone Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:30
Board of Equalization314-615-7195boe@stlouiscountymo.govSame schedule as the Assessor
Collector of Revenue314-615-7100collector@stlouiscountymo.govCounter Mon to Thu 8:00 to 3:30

The Collector bills for more than 200 taxing districts, so two homes in the same city can receive very different totals. Go through the district list on your bill line by line, because each line is a separate taxing body.

No Missouri county is bigger: 1,004,125 people in the 2020 count, and an estimated 990,911 on July 1, 2025 (down 1.4%). Housing runs to 448,637 units and 413,849 households, about 69.2% of them owner-occupied. The typical owned home is worth $276,800, the median rent is $1,209, and the median household makes $82,936. People commute 23.1 minutes on average.

Inside the county are dozens of municipalities and 23 public school districts, among them Rockwood, Parkway, Lindbergh, Mehlville, Pattonville, Ritenour and Ferguson-Florissant. The school levy on a bill can differ a lot between neighbors.

Missouri law has the County Assessor reassess all real estate countywide in each odd-numbered year, which puts the next round in 2027.

Check the value and property class on a new notice against what you know of the house. If something looks off, phone the Assessor at 314-615-2555 while the appeal window is still open. The Assessor answers value questions by phone on weekdays, while in-person visits run Monday through Thursday.

Value disputes go to the Board of Equalization, a body independent of the Assessor. It takes cases from homeowners, businesses and manufacturers, and it also reviews exemption requests from not-for-profit organizations. Contact it at 314-615-7195 or boe@stlouiscountymo.gov.

  • Deadline: under RSMo 137.275 the board must have your appeal by the second Monday in July. That falls on July 12 in 2027.
  • Method: you may appeal in person, through an attorney or agent, or in writing.
  • Burden of proof: RSMo 138.060 gives the assessor's number no presumption of correctness, and in a charter county of more than one million people the assessor has to show the value is no higher than true market value. The board can explain how this applies to you.
  • Next step: the State Tax Commission hears appeals from the board's decision. Ask the board for its current filing instructions.

Evidence for a lower figure can include a recent appraisal, your purchase contract, comparable sales or repair estimates.

Penalties start after January 1. RSMo 139.100 tells the Collector to charge a penalty on unpaid tax from the day after the first of January, at the rate in RSMo 140.100: 18% of each year's delinquency for land in the back tax book. Land redeemed ahead of a sale cannot be charged more than 2% for each month or part of a month.

A mailed payment is treated as paid on its postmark date, and certified or registered mail counts from the date of registration. With a postmark inside the allowed period, no extra tax or penalty applies. The Collector's page links to a Pay Taxes page, a tax rates lookup and a customer service portal at csportal.stlouiscountymo.gov.

If your bill looks wrong, call 314-615-7100 before you pay, and keep any corrected statement with your closing papers.

Every closing in the county touches the tax bill. The title company asks for a payoff or a proration for the current year, and an unpaid earlier year carries the 18% penalty described above. Request your parcel's balance from the Collector and pass that number to the closing agent.

If a lender pays your tax from escrow, confirm that the last bill was paid before you list. If a senior tax freeze is on your account, ask the Collector how it is treated when the property changes hands.

Delinquent parcels go to a county tax sale, which the Collector also runs. With the counter closed Fridays and weekends, a seller who wants a payoff letter that week should call early or pay by mail or online. If you are behind, phone 314-615-7100 for payoff figures and sale dates rather than waiting for a notice.

Back tax comes out of your proceeds at closing, so it will not stop a sale. It can slow one if nobody requests the payoff early. Cash buyers do not wait for a lender, which helps if you are working against a deadline. Weigh each offer against what a standard listing would leave after commission and repairs, and see that the settlement statement shows the tax line cleared.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
1. Read your parcel's value and property class on the Assessor's notice, and call 314-615-2555 if either looks wrong.
  2. Look at the district lines on your latest bill so you can tell buyers which schools and services come with the address.
  3. Get the parcel's balance from the Collector, older years included, and pay whatever is overdue so the 18% penalty stops growing.
  4. If your lender escrows the tax, confirm the last bill was paid.
  5. If an appeal is on your list, pull together the evidence now.
  6. Hand the payoff figure to the closing agent, and keep the stamped envelope or receipt for any payment you mail.

Settling a delinquent account early is worth the effort, because a buyer's title company will not close until the tax line is clear and the Collector can only confirm a payoff figure during office hours. A seller who handles this a week or two before the closing date avoids a last-minute scramble.

Counter hours in Clayton run only Monday through Thursday, so plan any in-person errand early in the week. Most questions can be handled by phone or email without a trip downtown. When you call, have your parcel number or address ready, plus the bill or notice you are asking about.

faqs.a: Third floor of 41 South Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. Phones are staffed 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, and the counter is open Monday through Thursday, 8:00 to 3:30.
The Board of Equalization, reached at 314-615-7195 or boe@stlouiscountymo.gov. It operates apart from the Assessor and takes appeals from homeowners, businesses and manufacturers.

faqs.q: What is the filing cutoff for an appeal?
faqs.a: Missouri statute fixes it at the second Monday of July, which is July 12 in 2027. You may appear yourself, send an agent or attorney, or file in writing.

faqs.q: Do all St. Louis County owners pay the same rate?
faqs.a: No. More than 200 taxing districts appear in the Collector's system, and the ones that cover your parcel set what you owe. A house in one school district can pay differently from a similar house in the next.

faqs.q: Does a postmark on the last day count?
faqs.a: Yes, if it travels by U.S. mail. RSMo 139.100 treats the postmark date as the payment date, and certified or registered mail uses the date of registration. Keep the stamped envelope or receipt.
